analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR: SHARP REVERSAL (U.S. Equities Color, 19 Nov 2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 closed -202bps at 7,175 with a market-on-close imbalance of $5.6bn to buy. NDX closed -221bps at 26,517, R2K -202bps at 2,659 and Dow -219bps at 49,097.
Equities finished on the lows after a ~400bp intra-day fade. NDX is now up 5% YTD. No single headline drove the sell-off. Some participants pointed to an AMD short report that weighed on sentiment.
The desk describes the tape as more questions than answers, with most clients asking what would make it feel better.
Volume was 20.873bn shares across all US equity exchanges versus a YTD daily average of 18.566bn. The floor rated activity a 7 out of 10 outside of capital markets activity.
Asset managers and hedge funds net sold macro products and net bought pockets of consumer and financials. No sector screened materially for sale.
Liquidity is poor and is exacerbating price action. S&P top-of-book depth averaged just $4mm at the touch.
The largest IPO in history debuted today and saw robust demand from a variety of client types. Spot and vol then rallied hard on the sell-off after the IPO open.
Single-stock earnings: INTC +2%, PANW +6% on earnings. After the bell, ESTC -8% and INTU -13%.
Spot VIX closed at 28.65, sharply inverted, and traded more than 4 vol points over UX1. This is the most inverted VIX term structure since April 2025.

Flows in derivatives were quiet in size but defined by put and put spread buying. The desk saw no appetite to fade the move. SPX and NDX fixed strike vols were bid, with gamma tenors closing just under +1 vol.
The desk estimates dealers are right around max short vega going into regular expiry tomorrow. It says the market needs some of those options unwound to settle into a more stable equilibrium.

market_movers.rationale: Some market participants pointed to an AMD short report as a factor that tapered overall sentiment. The note does not size AMD's own move.
INTC closed +2% on a day the S&P fell 202bps.
PANW rose 6% on earnings. The note gives no EPS or revenue figures.
ESTC fell 8% after the bell on its earnings release. The note gives no EPS or revenue figures.
INTU fell 13% after the bell on its earnings release. The note gives no EPS or revenue figures.

earnings_insights: PANW reported earnings and closed +2% to +6% range as stated: +6% on the day. The note gives no EPS or revenue figures or consensus comparison.
Post-bell reactions to reported earnings on 11/19: ESTC -8% and INTU -13% after hours. No EPS basis, adjusted versus reported, or consensus is given.
INTC closed +2%. The note does not tie the move to a stated earnings event.
crypto_views: Bitcoin closed -48bps. The note prints the level as $61,9556, which appears to be a typo and is not a clean price.
risk_factors: Poor liquidity is exacerbating price action, with S&P top-of-book depth at $4mm.
Dealers are around max short vega into tomorrow's regular expiry, and the desk says the market needs options unwound before it can settle.
No clear single driver of the sell-off, so there is no identified catalyst to reverse it.
A short report on AMD was cited by some as weighing on sentiment.
vol_and_positioning: Spot VIX closed +1665bps at 28.65, sharply inverted. It traded more than 4 vol points over UX1, the most inverted term structure since April 2025.
The tomorrow straddle on SPX prices a 1.43% move. Short-dated options are pricing a great deal of fear.
SPX and NDX fixed strike vols were bid. Gamma tenors closed just under +1 vol.
Spot and vol ranges were extremely wide. The straddle high to low was realized multiple times on the day.
Options flow was categorized by put and put spread buying with no appetite seen to fade the move. A VIX Dec put tree was bought 20k times as a vol-lower trade.
The desk estimates it is right around max dealer short vega going into regular expiry tomorrow. It says some options need to be unwound for a more stable equilibrium.
Positioning flows: asset managers and hedge funds net sold macro products and net bought pockets of consumer and financials.
Market depth is thin. S&P top-of-book averaged just $4mm at the touch.
